description: Tool for shell commands execution, visualization and alerting. Configured with a simple YAML file.

summary.one_liner: Sampler is a terminal tool that runs shell commands on a schedule and visualizes their output as charts, gauges, and text boxes, with optional alerts, configured through a YAML file.
summary.what_it_does: Sampler takes shell commands defined in a YAML config file, executes each one at a set rate (rate-ms), and renders the output in the terminal UI. Available components are runchart (line chart), sparkline, barchart, gauge, textbox, and asciibox (large ASCII text). Triggers fire visual, terminal-bell, sound, or arbitrary-script actions when a condition command returns true. Interactive shell support uses init (run once), sample (run repeatedly), and transform (post-process output) commands, so a database or SSH session can be opened once and polled. Variables, environment variables, and a light or dark color theme are also supported.
use_cases: Watch a metric from a shell command in the terminal
Poll a database value over time without setting up Grafana
Track Docker container CPU and memory stats
Run and watch a remote server's top output over SSH
Get an alert when a latency or threshold is exceeded
how_to_run: Download the binary to /usr/local/bin/sampler and chmod +x it (Linux/macOS)
Write a config.yml defining components and sample commands
stack: ALSA library (libasound2-dev) on Linux for trigger sound
notable: No servers, databases, or deployment needed; just shell commands and a YAML file
Interactive shell mode (init/sample/transform) keeps a database or SSH session open between samples
Triggers can ring the terminal bell, play a NASA quindar tone, show a visual alert, or run a script
Can sample multiple remote machines from a local instance via ssh in init commands
Real-world recipes for MySQL, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Neo4j, Kafka, Docker, SSH, and JMX
caveats: Windows support is marked experimental and recommended only with advanced console emulators
Linux sound triggers require the libasound2-dev system library
Not a replacement for full-scale monitoring systems like Prometheus with Grafana
